newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Sierra Leone wants U.N. observers for peace accord.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone wants U.N. observers for peace accord.

text.p: Sierra Leone has requested U.N. observers to monitor the implementation of its recent peace agreement, the president of the Security Council said on Tuesday.
U.N. officials said they expected a letter from the government shortly and presumed the request was for military observers.
"Authorities in that country have requested the U.N. to send observers," Council President Paolo Fulci of Italy said after a meeting of the 15-member council.
"There is a huge problem of displaced people, 40 percent of the entire population is displaced," he added.
The government and rebels signed a peace accord on Nov. 30 to end their six-year old civil war in the West African country which took the lives of at least 10,000 people.

Earlier this week unknown gunmen were reported to have killed about 150 people in attacks on two communes in northern Sierra Leone. But the government denied the report, saying it had no evidence to confirm it and that such news could undermine its peace deal with rebels.
